description: 3.3V Transceiver 12Mbps 32 SOP-8 Drivers, Receivers, Transceivers RoHS

parameters.Features: Tx/Rx enable;Enable shutdown;Overcurrent Protection;Thermal shutdown protection

provenance.pins: datasheet p.3 PIN DESCRIPTION table (SOP-8). vMax values are from p.2 Absolute Maximum Ratings, not from the pin table.

designVerdict: SELECTED - differential data link, 2 off (one per channel)
notes: MAX3485, 3.3 V differential line transceiver (RS-485 levels), SOP-8, 6.6k stock, $0.35. Cheaper than the SN65HVD75 (C57928, $0.59) that was the earlier candidate, and in JLCPCB's assembly catalogue.
Runs from 3.3 V, so the ESP32-C6 drives DI directly - no level shifting on the data path at the controller end.

Data is one-way, so DE is tied high. RE_N is tied high too: RE is active-low, so high DISABLES the receiver, and 'unused' is not a state for a CMOS input. Two needed, one per channel, since each chain carries different pixel data.
Needs a matching receiver and 120 ohm termination on the first converter board of each chain. Populating only the controller end is useless.
800 kbps WS2812 timing is far inside its 10 Mbps capability.
TERMINOLOGY: called a differential pair in the design docs. RS-485 line levels, but no RS-485 connector convention - the pair runs over two poles of a picoMAX next to power and ground.

THIS IS A JSMSEMI CLONE, not a Maxim part, and that fact qualifies every number in this record. Its switching table (12/15 Mbps) and ESD claims appear copied from the MAX3485E while it is sold under the plain CSA suffix; the genuine CSA is the 10 Mbps non-E part with no ESD specification at all.

LCSC PARAMETERS ARE WRONG HERE, and kb.py add will reimpose them on every refresh: 'Quiescent Supply Current 500uA' is 4x optimistic (p.4 gives I_CC max 2000 uA with DE high, 1500 uA with DE low; the 500 uA is p.1 prose for a DISABLED driver), and 'Features: Enable shutdown' has no basis - there is no shutdown mode, no shutdown current and no RE/DE combination with a reduced-current rating anywhere in the document. 'Data Rate 12Mbps' is the TYP column; the guaranteed figure is the 10 Mbps minimum.

NO GUARANTEES AWAY FROM 25 C. Both the DC and AC tables are headed 'VCC = 3.3V, TA = 25C'; Maxim's original specifies over TMIN-TMAX. The -40/+85 C in Recommended Operating Conditions is a functional range with nothing electrical behind it. There is also no theta-JA, no package derating and no thermal-shutdown trip point despite p.1 claiming the feature - so a junction-temperature calculation on this part cannot be closed from its own datasheet, on a board whose thermal section already calls the enclosure case over budget.

V_OD is specified only at 50 ohm (1.0 V min) and 27 ohm (0.6 V min). There is no 54 ohm or 120 ohm figure, the two minima are not physically self-consistent, and p.9's prose claim of '>1.5 V at 54 ohm' contradicts the p.4 table. The link works - 1.0 V against a +/-200 mV threshold - by inference, not by spec. The argument that actually holds for WS2812 timing is t_SKEW 10 ns max against a +/-150 ns window, not the data-rate headline.

rules.note: driver enable must be driven or strapped; this design ties DE high AND RE_N high - RE is active-low, so high disables the receiver, which is what an unused CMOS input needs. The line is never idle.
